## TypeScript

- Prefer `bun` for package and script workflows.
- Keep code strict-friendly.
- Avoid implicit `any`, unnecessary explicit `any`, and non-null assertions.
- Type weakly-contextual callbacks and public data shapes.
- Prefer schema validation for external/untrusted data (Zod `.safeParse()`,
  returning structured errors rather than throwing).

### TypeScript observability spellings

> **`rtech-standards` is canonical.** The TypeScript binding is
> `@rtech/obs` (`rtech-standards/packages/typescript`, tracked as
> rtech-standards#2, gated on the Bun transport spike rtech-standards#3). The
> spellings below describe how a TypeScript service satisfies the
> language-neutral requirements above; the wire format itself comes from
> `OBSERVABILITY_CONTRACT.md`. Anything here that conflicts with the contract
> loses.

Implements `## Observability` above. `king-capital/docs/coding-standards.md` is
the proven source for these rules; repo-local standards may be stricter but must
not weaken them.

**Target state: a shared package, not nine implementations.** These rules
describe what that package does. A document that asks nine repos to each build
their own logger produces nine field vocabularies and fractures the Loki query
surface; a package produces one. Follow the `@king/core` precedent — shared
concerns live in a package and are never duplicated per repo. Until it exists,
implement the shape below and expect to delete it in favour of the import.

The package owns four exports and nothing more. Feature growth is how a shared
utility becomes something people work around:

| Export | Loguru equivalent | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `logger` | `from loguru import logger` | preconfigured; no assembly at call sites |
| `withContext(fields, fn)` | `contextualize()` | binds `correlation_id` across `await` |
| `withLogging(name, fn)` | `@logger.catch` + five points | entry/exit/duration/failure, re-throws |
| `initObservability()` | `logger.add(...)` | one call at boot; sinks, level, redaction |

Rules:

- **Pino only. Never `console.log`/`warn`/`error`** outside the logging module
  itself.
- **Pino's level names must be remapped to the contract's.** Pino emits `warn`
  and `fatal`; the contract requires `warning` and `critical` (Loki matches
  literally, and the fixture rejects the abbreviations). The binding owns this
  mapping via a `customLevels`/formatter so call sites never see the difference.
- **Writes must not block the caller on I/O.** Use Pino's worker-thread
  transport; this is the `enqueue=True` requirement. A synchronous write on a
  request path is a violation even when the output is otherwise correct. Note the
  Python reference measured ~50 µs/record still spent inline on serialization and
  redaction — "does not block on I/O" is the honest claim, not "free", and the TS
  binding's real cost must be measured (rtech-standards#3), not assumed.
- One preconfigured `logger` export per service. No logger assembly at call
  sites.
- Bind per-operation context with child loggers (`rootLogger.child({ service })`)
  rather than repeating fields at every call.
- Carry `correlation_id` across `await` boundaries with `AsyncLocalStorage`. A
  correlation id that has to be threaded by hand will be dropped somewhere.
- **Prefer a wrapper over discipline.** `withLogging()` is the TypeScript
  `@logger.catch`: it emits entry, exit with duration, and failure, then
  re-throws. Wrapping an operation once is the compliant path; remembering five
  calls at every site is the path that has already failed at scale.
- **The package stamps the envelope fields**, callers never supply them.
  `timestamp`, `level`, `service`, `host`, and `message` are owned by the package
  (contract §1.3). Caller-supplied envelope fields get spelled differently in
  every repo and split the query surface. Unknown top-level fields are relocated
  into `context` rather than accepted.
- `catch (error: unknown)` — narrow before use. Never `catch (e: any)` and never
  `error as Error`.
- Never spread a raw error object into a log entry; it can carry attached
  request, credential, or payload data. Serialize a chosen subset.
- Configuration owned by the package and validated at boot, failing closed on
  invalid input. The contract's variables (§5) are `SERVICE_NAME`, `LOG_LEVEL`,
  `LOG_FILE`, and `LOG_STDOUT`, read in one place and frozen — not scattered as
  `process.env` reads. Missing `SERVICE_NAME` or an invalid `LOG_LEVEL` raises; an
  unwritable `LOG_FILE` degrades to stdout with one loud warning, because a
  service must not fail to boot over an absent log mount.
- Process-level `uncaughtException` and `unhandledRejection` handlers registered
  by `initObservability()`, logging before exit.
- Public functions and modules documented with TSDoc (`@param`, `@returns`,
  `@throws`) at the same bar as Google-style docstrings in Python.

Lint spellings for the enforcement rules above: `no-empty` (catch blocks),
`@typescript-eslint/no-floating-promises`, `no-console` outside the logging
module, `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any`, plus the custom
catch-body-must-log-or-rethrow rule.

Shape at a call site — this is the whole surface a service author sees:

```ts
// boot, once
initObservability();

// per request or per operation, at the boundary
await withContext({ correlation_id: requestId }, async () => {
  await withLogging("lane_context_load", async () => {
    // ... work. entry/exit/duration/failure already logged.
    // a degraded path still logs explicitly:
    if (!lane) {
      logger.warning("no lane matched the session scope", {
        event: "lane_scope_miss",
        session_key,
      });
    }
  });
});
```

`event` is the **stable machine-readable name** (`lane_scope_miss`) and is what
Loki aggregates on; `message` is the human-readable sentence you actually read in
a post-mortem. The contract carries both because they do different jobs — prose
alone is not queryable, and an event name alone tells you nothing at 3am.

Note the level is `warning`, not `warn`. Loki matches level values literally, so
the abbreviated JS spelling is non-conforming (contract §1.3).

**Accepted gap:** Loguru's `diagnose` — tracebacks carrying variable *values* at
each frame — has no JavaScript equivalent in any library. Do not go looking.
